title: EXECUTIVE ENGINEER ELECTRICAL versus VIKAS KUMAR

paras.text:
UKHC010167292026
2026:UHC:9387
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2872 of 2026 (M/S)
Executive Engineer Electrical ........Petitioner

Versus
Vikas Kumar and Another ........Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Piyush Tiwari, Central Government Council for the petitioner.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
By means of the instant petition, the petitioner seeks the
following reliefs:-
i) Issue a writ or order in the nature of certiorari quashing
impugned order dated 23.06.2026 (Being Annexure No.-11)
(Page 131 to 132) passed by the learned Deputy Chief Labour
Commissioner (Central), Dehradun/Appellate Authority.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certiorari
quashing order dated 12.12.2024 (being Annexure No.-6)
(Page 89 to 97) passed by the learned Assistant Labour
Commissioner (Central), Dehradun/Controlling Authority,
whereby the liability towards payment of gratuity to
respondent no.1 has been fastened upon the petitioner
Department.
iii) Issue any other writ, order or direction which this hon'ble
Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and
circumstances of the case.
iv) Award the cost of the writ petition to the petitioner.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the
record.

2
3. An order was passed by the Controlling Authority Under
Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 and Assistant Labour Commissioner
(Central) Dehradun on 12.12.2024 in Claim Application No. D-36(PG-254) 2023-ALC, Shri Vikas Kumar v. The Executive Engineer and
Another, against which an appeal was filed by the petitioner before the
Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Dehradun ("the appeal").
The appeal was dismissed on 23.06.2026 on the ground of delay.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there
were total 29 appeals that were filed before the office of Deputy Chief
Labour Commissioner (Central) Dehradun, and all the appeals were
dismissed. Against 28 appeals, WPMS No.2873 of 2026, Executive
Engineer Electrical Dehradun v. Nand Gopal Yadav, and connected
petitions were filed, which have already been dismissed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court by the order dated 07.10.2026 ("the
first petition"). It is argued that the issue is identical.
5. In its order dated 07.10.2026, passed in the first petition,
the Coordinate Bench of this Court observed as follows:-
"14. In the present case, order was passed by
Controlling Authority on 18.12.2024 and appeal against the
order passed by Controlling Authority was filed on
31.10.2025; the memo of appeal filed by petitioner is
absolutely silent regarding 'cause of delay', and the factum of
composite appeal, filed by petitioner against 29 orders and
return of such appeal by the Appellate Authority vide letter
dated 10.10.2025, is also not mentioned. Thus, the reliance
by petitioner on the aforesaid judgment is clearly misplaced.
15. Provisions of Limitation Act do not apply to
proceedings under Payment of Gratuity Act, therefore, there
is no question of filing a delay condonation application under
Section 5 of the Limitation Act in proceedings under Payment
of Gratuity Act. As per Statutory Scheme, appeal against
order passed under Section 7(4) of Payment of Gratuity Act
has to be filed within sixty days from the date of receipt of
order, however, the limitation period is extendable for a

3
further period of sixty days. An appeal filed after 120 days
from the date of receipt of the order, however, cannot be
entertained, as the Appellate Authority has not been
conferred the power to condone such delay."
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner admits that the memo
of appeal filed by the petitioner is absolutely silent regarding the cause
of delay and the factum of composite appeal filed by the petitioner
against 29 orders and return of such appeal by the appellate authority
is also not mentioned in the memo of appeals. He submits that there
were some reference to it.
6. The Coordinate Bench of this Court has already held in
the first petition that an appeal filed after 120 days from the date of
receipt of the order, cannot be entertained, and the appellate
authority, under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, has not been
conferred any power to condone the delay.
8. This Court has no reason to take a different view. The
matter is squarely covered by the judgment and order dated
07.10.2026, passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the first
petition. Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
 14.10.2026
Ravi Bisht
